basis: Immunodeficiency, bronchiectasis and inflammatory gastrointestinal disease are defining features; bronchiectasis 3/3, oral ulcers 2/2 and esophageal stricture 1/1.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: recurrent pulmonary infections leading to bronchiectasis explicitly define the disease; bronchiectasis reported in 3/3.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: inflammatory gastrointestinal disease is explicitly defining, supported by oral ulceration 2/2 and esophageal stricture 1/1.

basis: Lysosomal storage disease defined by progressive neurodegeneration and early retinal degeneration; visual loss occurs in nearly all classic juvenile CLN3 cases.

decisions.ocular: primary: early progressive retinal degeneration and visual loss are defining clinical features of classic juvenile CLN3 disease.

basis: Locally aggressive neoplasm arising in bone; endothelial histology does not establish additional cardiovascular organ involvement.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: the tumour's anatomical origin is bone; endothelial differentiation alone does not establish a separate cardiovascular site.

basis: Recurrent hepatic cholestasis from defective bile transport; hearing impairment and pancreatitis have unspecified frequencies. Jaundice and pruritus do not establish eye or skin damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: this is a hepatic bile transport disorder; neither inheritance nor secondary bilirubin accumulation establishes an additional metabolic disorder.

basis: Hypomyelination and neurodegeneration define disease. Scoliosis and ptosis, each 1/1, do not establish direct extra-neural damage rather than consequences of severe motor dysfunction.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis in 1/1 is compatible with neurological motor dysfunction; direct ocular injury or impaired vision is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis in 1/1 accompanies severe spastic tetraplegia; evidence does not establish direct skeletal or muscle disease.

basis: Metabolic enzyme deficiency with acidosis; hepatic dysfunction and rhabdomyolysis are reported, but frequencies and status as major diagnostic criteria are unspecified.

decisions.hepatic: none: decreased liver function is reported without a frequency or established major diagnostic-criterion status; the 30% threshold is unsupported.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: rhabdomyolysis represents muscle damage, but its frequency and status as a major diagnostic criterion are unspecified.

basis: The supplied umbrella definition specifies progressive muscle degeneration and weakness; direct peripheral nerve, CNS or neuromuscular junction pathology is subtype dependent.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurological ancestry does not establish neural damage across most patients; the supplied definition specifies muscle degeneration.

basis: Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the disorder; strabismus in 2/2 assessed patients supports ocular alignment dysfunction, with uncertainty from the small sample.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus documents ocular alignment dysfunction in 2/2 assessed patients; supplied frequency supports inclusion, although the sample is small.

basis: Defining CNS, pituitary and skeletal abnormalities; anal atresia 30-79%. Cap omits airway, renal, ocular and ear defects (30-79%) and nail dysplasia (8/12); bifid epiglottis often asymptomatic.

decisions.pulmonary: none at cap: bifid epiglottis 13/18 is often asymptomatic; laryngeal cleft 30-79% supports airway involvement, but obstructive anal atresia takes priority.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: anal atresia is a major syndrome feature reported in 30-79%, with direct intestinal obstruction; retained for severity within the four-axis cap.

basis: Eyelids explicitly belong to the ocular axis; most eyelid neoplasms arise in eyelid skin, also supported by the skin-neoplasm parent.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: most tumours across this umbrella originate in eyelid skin; the explicit skin-neoplasm parent supports dermatologic alongside ocular classification.
